basics.label: Software Engineer · MSc CS @ IST · Lisbon

narratives.headline: I turn manual, spreadsheet-driven processes into reliable web systems.
narratives.short: I'm Francisca Almeida, a full-stack engineer working in TypeScript/Next.js, Python/FastAPI and PostgreSQL. Currently shipping Odoo ERP migrations at ThinkOpen Solutions. Until mid-2026 I led the dev team at SINFO, where I rebuilt the conference website that drew 14.3k visits in the event month.
narratives.detailed:
I'm a full-stack engineer and MSc student in Computer Science and Engineering at Instituto Superior Técnico, based in Lisbon. Most of my work has the same shape: a process that lives in spreadsheets, forms and manual steps, turned into a system people can rely on. At Micro Harvest that was an operations dashboard replacing Excel workflows. At ThinkOpen Solutions it is Odoo ERP migrations and AI-agent workflows that automate test planning, execution and reporting.

Until July 2026 I led the development team at SINFO, Portugal's largest free tech conference, where I rebuilt the website and the campaign-attribution analytics behind it. I also contribute fixes to open-source projects I use, and I care about measurable results and about leaving codebases easier to change than I found them.

Away from the keyboard, though rarely far from it: I'm learning the electric drums, pick up the harmonica once in a while, and do jigsaw puzzles when I need to slow down. A weekly padel lesson turned into a smartwatch app that keeps score during the game, and a mini pedal exerciser under my desk now drives in-game movement through a Bluetooth sensor. The rest is series, films and games: The Last of Us, Red Dead Redemption 2 and the Life is Strange series are all-time favourites.

star_highlights.situation: SINFO needed a reliable web app and website for Portugal's largest free tech conference.

star_highlights.result: 1,400+ attendees served during the conference; the rebuilt website drew 14.3k visits in the event month.

projects.title: SINFO Website Rebuild
projects.description: Next.js platform for Portugal's largest free tech conference, rebuilt from the ground up with a modular component system and campaign-attribution analytics.
projects.problem: The legacy site was hard to change and nobody could tell which campaigns actually brought attendees.
projects.solution: Rebuilt the site on Next.js App Router, TypeScript and Tailwind as a modular component system for schedule, speakers and sponsors. Dockerised staging and production. Added referral attribution through ref query params feeding Grafana dashboards. Led a team of junior developers: scope, timelines and mentoring.
projects.result: Served SINFO 33 in April 2026: 14.3k visits in the event month, 6,000+ visits and 10,000+ page views per month since. 35+ commits merged upstream.

projects.title: NEIIST Merch Store
projects.description: End-to-end e-commerce for a student association: catalogue, cart, checkout and an admin area with order management and Excel export.
projects.problem: Merch orders were collected through forms and reconciled by hand in spreadsheets.
projects.solution: Built the catalogue, cart, checkout and an admin area with order management and Excel export (ExcelJS) on the existing React, Express and PostgreSQL codebase. Shipped as 8 merged pull requests, including the mobile cart fixes.
projects.result: 220+ orders processed through the store, with order exports replacing manual spreadsheet reconciliation.

open_source.description: Fixed a UX bug where the inbox-zero celebration showed on non-inbox tabs. The first version added a prop to the Celebration component; after maintainer feedback, shipped a simpler message-only solution.

Resolved a critical state rendering bug in the student-led schedule builder where timetable lessons would intermittently disappear. Fixed the identification logic by replacing non-unique class name identifiers with unique IDs, eliminating rendering collisions during view updates and filter changes.
